episode.title: Strip truncated tool-argument fragments prefixed by a bare tool name
episode.before: At parent commit 41c17d9b5e1299b404700f86d6abad5cd406f3b6, the unterminated-tool-call sanitizer recognized argument-tag fragments only when an <arg_key> or <arg_value> tag itself began the line (apart from whitespace), or when an argument closer ended the line. A truncated serialization such as "process_manage<arg_key>action</arg_key>..." therefore escaped sanitization because the bare tool name preceded the first tag.
episode.after: At cf8b08edac3a78feb4b9db0c20a62934c3a6c49d, the line-boundary alternative accepts an optional prefix composed only of identifier-like characters [\w.:-] before an argument tag. Both display and storage sanitizers consequently remove bare-name-prefixed truncated tool-call fragments while retaining preceding visible text; existing tests continue to require that prose containing spaced inline argument-tag examples and subsequent prose remain intact.
episode.diff: The implementation changed one regular-expression alternative from matching optional whitespace immediately followed by an argument tag to matching optional whitespace, then zero or more identifier-like characters, then the tag. Comments document the bounded prefix and prose-preservation intent. Two parameterized regression cases were added: one complete name-prefixed argument fragment and one fragment cut inside its argument value. The cases run against both the final-display sanitizer and the stored-content sanitizer.

evidence_units.claim: The parent implementation required an arg_key or arg_value tag to appear directly at a line boundary after optional whitespace, so its fragment alternative did not admit a bare tool-name prefix.
The pinned change inserted [\w.:-]* before the argument tag in the unterminated-fragment alternative, allowing an identifier-only prefix while excluding prefixes containing spaces.
The changed pattern is included in the ordered stripping-pattern collection, and strip_think_blocks applies every pattern by substitution to visible content.

The regression suite defines display and storage stripper variants and applies the fragment cases to both, establishing that the shared behavior is required at final display and stored-content boundaries.
Two added cases require a complete bare-name-prefixed argument fragment and a fragment cut inside an argument value to be removed while preserving the preceding visible line.
Neighboring tests require inline prose with argument tags, later prose, and ordinary complete-block handling to survive appropriately, constraining the matcher against broad deletion.
The commit states that name-prefixed cut calls leaked raw markup and that only an identifier-only prefix should be allowed so prose such as "The <arg_key> holds..." survives.

The evidence bundle resolves issue/PR 101899 to the pinned commit, records parent 41c17d9b5e1299b404700f86d6abad5cd406f3b6, and identifies the implementation and regression-test files as the only changed files.

candidate_atomics.name: bound-name-prefixed-structured-fragment-matching
candidate_atomics.title: Recognize name-prefixed structured-call fragments without consuming prose
candidate_atomics.description: Extend a line-oriented malformed-call detector to admit only an identifier-like prefix attached directly to an argument tag, preserving its existing line boundary and prose-safety constraints.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent raw structured-call argument markup from reaching visible or stored assistant text when a truncated serialization begins with a bare tool name.
semantic_action.module_role: Malformed structured-output sanitizer shared by assistant-content consumers
semantic_action.pre_state: A line contains a truncated argument-tag serialization whose first tag is glued to a bare identifier-like call name, and the sanitizer only recognizes tags that directly begin the line.
semantic_action.post_state: The name-prefixed fragment is classified as unrecoverable structured output and removed, while prefixes containing prose-separating spaces remain outside this new match shape.
semantic_action.validation: Apply the sanitizer to complete and cut name-prefixed fragments and verify that only the preceding visible text remains; also verify that spaced inline prose examples survive.

candidate_atomics.title: Verify malformed-fragment removal across display and storage boundaries
candidate_atomics.description: Encode the malformed inputs and preservation expectations once, then exercise both consumer-facing sanitizers to prevent their structured-output contracts from diverging.

semantic_action.intent: Establish a regression oracle showing that every relevant assistant-content boundary removes the newly recognized malformed fragments without broadening deletion into ordinary prose.

semantic_action.post_state: Both display and storage sanitizer variants are checked against complete and cut name-prefixed fragments, and preservation tests constrain false-positive removal.
semantic_action.validation: Run the parameterized fragment test for both sanitizer variants and the adjacent prose-preservation tests; the expected outputs retain visible prefixes and remove malformed markup.

candidate_workflows.name: repair-leaking-truncated-structured-call-fragments
candidate_workflows.title: Repair leaked truncated tool-call fragments while preserving ordinary prose
candidate_workflows.description: A bounded workflow for a sanitizer that already removes malformed structured calls but misses a newly observed serialization prefix. It narrows the grammar change to the smallest evidenced prefix class and validates both removal and non-removal behavior across content consumers.

workflow_graph.goal: Remove unrecoverable name-prefixed structured-call fragments from assistant content at every relevant sanitization boundary without deleting natural-language mentions or later unrelated prose.
when_to_use: A structured-output sanitizer already handles line-leading argument tags, but raw markup leaks when the first tag is directly attached to a bare identifier-like call name.
The malformed fragment is unrecoverable and should be removed rather than parsed or executed.
More than one consumer boundary is expected to enforce the same stripping contract.
anti_goals: Do not interpret, reconstruct, or execute the truncated call.
Do not accept arbitrary prose before an argument tag as a fragment prefix.
Do not remove unrelated preceding or subsequent visible prose.
Do not redesign complete structured-call parsing or unrelated reasoning-tag handling.
not_applicable_when: The input is a complete, valid structured call that should be parsed through the normal tool-call path.
The suspected prefix contains spaces or sentence text and cannot be distinguished from an inline prose example by the evidenced identifier-only rule.
The affected consumer does not use the shared line-oriented stripping contract.
There is no reproducible malformed input and preservation oracle.
inputs: The set of display and storage sanitizer consumers
Positive removal expectations and negative prose-preservation examples
workflow_graph.entry_state: Raw argument markup from a truncated structured call can survive because a bare call name appears immediately before the first argument tag, while existing behavior already protects ordinary inline prose.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Identifier-only name-prefixed fragments are removed by all tested sanitizer consumers, preceding visible text is retained, and spaced inline prose plus unrelated trailing prose remain protected.

steps.condition: The failing sample has a line-boundary identifier-like prefix directly glued to an arg_key or arg_value tag.
steps.validation: The matcher admits the observed complete and value-truncated prefixed shapes, while its prefix character class cannot span spaces into ordinary prose.

steps.condition: Display and storage paths are both contractually expected to strip tool-call markup.
steps.validation: Parameterized cases produce only the visible prefix for both sanitizer variants, and prose-preservation cases remain unchanged.

validation_ladder: Confirm the parent matcher excludes the captured name-prefixed shape.
Check the revised grammar admits only the evidenced identifier-like attached prefix.
Verify complete and value-truncated name-prefixed fragments are removed while their preceding visible lines remain.
Run the same cases against display and storage sanitizers.
Verify inline prose containing argument tags and subsequent unrelated prose survive.
stop_conditions: Stop if the prefix requires whitespace or arbitrary sentence text; the evidenced bounded grammar no longer distinguishes it safely from prose.
Stop if the fragment is recoverable through the normal complete-call parser rather than an unrecoverable sanitization case.
Stop if any preservation oracle shows deletion of ordinary prose or unrelated trailing content.
Stop before claiming runtime test success when the test runner is unavailable.

The exact implementation relationship of the display sanitizer to the changed shared pattern is established here through the dual-consumer regression contract, but its full source-level delegation path was not required by or changed in this commit.
